notes.content: Environmental Resource Management is an interdisciplinary major administered by the Dean of the School of Business and Public Administration. The major is a program of study that includes coursework in the following areas: Physical and life sciences relating to natural resource use; The legal aspects of resource ownership and use; The economic and political aspects of resource allocation and environmental protection; and Safety and environmental health concerns associated with resource use. The program also includes basic skills courses in areas such as communications, computers, statistics, and management. The ERM major is of sufficient breadth to prepare graduates for entry into a wide range of careers relating to the use, management, and protection of environmental assets. These careers are in areas such as resource analysis and planning, occupational safety, environmental health, compliance, technical and environmental staff support, permitting, and real estate development. Graduates typically find employment in both the private and public sectors. Public agencies such as the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the United States Forest Service (USFS) typically hire individuals with skills provided within the program. The program also requires a concentration (typically four courses), which further enhances the student experience. The concentration also gives students an opportunity to specialize in select areas. Concentrations can include Forestry, Environmental Health, Land Use Policy and Planning, and Occupational Safety and Health. In support of its commitment to community health and workplace safety, Aera Energy LLC has endowed a concentration in occupational health and safety management, a field with good internship and career opportunities. Internships are recommended for all concentrations. For additional information, visit the following: Department of Environmental Resource Management Program Requirements - Environmental Resource Management, BS, General Track

notes.content: Students who have taken Biology or Chemistry coursework should check the Articulation Agreement by the Department of the respective community colleges. The agreement may articulate differently, and it may determine whether the entire Biology and/or Chemistry sequence needs to be completed to receive appropriate course credit for the major requirements at CSUB.
